title: Set up the develop branch and git remote for the PR workflow
description:

CLAUDE.md's Git workflow needs a develop base branch and a remote: one worktree and branch per ticket from develop, pushed, with a PR into develop. Right now the repo has no remote, no develop, and its main branch is master, not main.

- [ ] Create develop (from master or wherever it should start)
- [ ] Add the git remote and make sure gh is authenticated
- [ ] Reconcile main vs master with what CLAUDE.md says
- [ ] Commit df2.2's leftovers on a chore/OrderList-df2.2-firebase-setup branch: package.json, package-lock.json (firebase-tools dev dependency) and docs/learning.md. They're currently uncommitted on research/android-delivery.

title: Adopt claude-starter agent workflow rules
description:
Adopt the reviewed rules from the claude-starter package (C:\Users\user\Downloads\claude-starter), adapted to this Expo repo.

## Decisions (agreed with user 2026-11-02)
- Integration branch `agents`: agent ticket PRs merge into `agents`; humans PR `agents` -> `develop`; `main` stays human-only. Main checkout stays on `agents`.
- Adopt `closer` and `cleaner` subagents (.claude/agents/). Closer is authorised to commit, push and merge into `agents`; one closer at a time. Branches never deleted.
- Worktrees in-repo: `.worktrees/<bead-id>` (short dir name, gitignored); branch keeps `<type>/<bead-id>-<slug>`. Worktree setup copies `.env.local` from the main checkout.
- Closer gates: `npm ci` -> `npx expo lint` -> `npx tsc --noEmit` -> `npx expo export`.
- Micro commits; run gates on branch tip and merge result only.
- Max 3 parallel agents.
- Closer runs `bd dolt push` after closing a bead (needs Dolt remote set up first, see below).
- Secrets: document existing setup - values in EAS env vars, pulled to gitignored `.env.local`; `EXPO_PUBLIC_` values ship in the bundle, never use for real secrets; never commit/print values.
- Docs: only `docs/nonfunctional-decisions.md` (created lazily). Not tech-stack, architecture, privacy, production-checklist.
- Keep `GLOSSARY.md` (not CONTEXT.md). Fix stale "no git remote" line in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md. wontfix beads are also closed. Skip starter's Code style section until an architecture ADR exists. Closer merges with `--merge`.

## To verify before/while implementing
- Exact `eas env:pull` command (EAS docs).
- Correct Dolt remote setup for refs/dolt/data (beads sync-concepts doc); `bd dolt remote add` warns when URL equals git origin. User runs setup.
- Whether Metro in the main checkout crawls `.worktrees/` (may need metro.config.js blockList).

## Needs user approval (outward-facing)
- Create and push `agents` branch from develop.
- Switch main checkout to `agents`.

2026-11-02: user dropped the agents integration branch for now - develop stays the base; closer/cleaner land on develop. Gates blocked by OrderList-94s (tsc) and OrderList-1ez (ESLint). Metro .worktrees/ exclusion deferred as OrderList-4yt. Dolt remote set up and verified (refs/dolt/data on origin).

description:

The Admin card gets a Shopping / By member switch for today's Order List. Shopping lists each Item with its total count across all Orders, so the Admin can buy without tallying. By member lists each Member with their Order, so the Admin can hand out the food. Both update live.

- [ ] By member shows each Member's display name with their Items, grouped by the case-insensitive Member key

title: Catalog suggestions and usual-Item chips
description:
## Parent

OrderList-df2 (spec: OrderList v1)

## What to build

Members can add Items without typing them out. While typing, Catalog suggestions appear and a tap adds one. Below the add box, "Your usuals" chips show Items this Member has ordered before and "Everything else" chips show the rest of the Catalog; tapping a chip adds that Item to My order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Suggestions match what's typed, case-insensitively, from the Catalog; tapping one adds it
- [ ] Adding an Item records it in the Member's usual Items
- [ ] Your usuals lists Items this Member ordered before; Everything else lists the rest of the Catalog, with no overlap
- [ ] Tapping a chip adds the Item; chips and suggestions are disabled when the Order List isn't Open
- [ ] The Catalog and chips update live when a teammate adds a new Item

title: Members add and remove Items by typing
description:
## Parent

OrderList-df2 (spec: OrderList v1)

## What to build

While today's Order List is Open, a Member types an Item name and presses add; it appears in My order, live. An exact case-insensitive match reuses the existing Catalog Item; any other name joins the Catalog. The same Item added twice shows twice; each entry has a remove button. While the Order List is Locked, the Security Rules refuse any change to Orders, and the Member sees why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Item names are trimmed; empty names are rejected
- [ ] An exact case-insensitive match reuses the Catalog Item (display name as first entered); otherwise a new Catalog Item is created
- [ ] The same Item added twice appears twice in My order; removing one leaves one
- [ ] My order shows only this Member's Items and updates live
- [ ] The add box and remove buttons are disabled when the Order List is Locked or there is no list today
- [ ] Rules refuse adding or removing while the Order List is Locked (one get() on the parent Order List); the Member sees an error; changes work again after unlock
- [ ] Any failed change shows an error (the app is online only)
- [ ] Emulator tests cover the criteria above through the module's public interface
- [ ] Updated Rules deployed to the real project (ask the person to run the deploy if the CLI isn't logged in)
- [ ] Lint, typecheck and tests pass

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Admin card shows Open when today has no Order List, otherwise Lock or Unlock for today's list
- [ ] Opening creates today's Order List as Open and, in the same write batch, locks any older Order List still Open
- [ ] A second Order List for the same day can't be opened
- [ ] Lock and unlock update the status pill live on every device

description:

On name entry, typing admin (any case) reveals a PIN field. The app reads the PIN from the Admin config document (collection config, document admin, field pin) and compares it on the device. A match makes this device the Admin until they switch name, and the Order screen shows an Admin card (empty for now). The Security Rules let clients read the PIN document but never write it.

- [ ] Members never see the Admin card

title: Spec: OrderList v1 (daily Order List on web + Android, Firebase Spark)
description:
## Problem Statement

Every day the Admin collects the team's food requests before going out to buy them. Today that happens by ad-hoc messages: requests get lost, arrive after the Admin has left, and the Admin has to tally them by hand into a shopping list. Members retype the same things every day and can't tell whether today's run is still taking requests.

## Solution

OrderList v1: one app on the web and on Android phones. The Admin opens today's Order List; Members type their name once, then add Items to their own Order, typing a name (with suggestions from the shared Catalog) or tapping one of their usual Items. When the Admin goes to buy, they lock the Order List so nothing changes under them, and they see a shopping view (totals per Item) and a per-Member view. Everyone sees changes live. Past Order Lists stay available to the Admin as read-only history.

The whole thing runs at $0: Firebase Spark (Firestore only, JS SDK, no Firebase Auth), the web app on EAS Hosting Free, and Android as an EAS internal-distribution APK kept current with EAS Update. Security is deliberately loose for an internal team tool.

## User Stories

Identity

1. As a Member, I want to type my name once on first launch, so that I can start ordering without creating an account.
2. As a Member, I want the app to remember my name on this device, so that I don't retype it every day.
3. As a Member, I want my name matched case-insensitively ("ahmed" = "Ahmed"), so that I keep the same Order and usual Items however I type it.
4. As a Member who shares a name with a teammate, I want to type a distinguishing name ("Ahmed K"), so that our Orders don't merge.
5. As a Member, I want to switch to a different name, so that I can fix a typo or hand the device to someone else.
6. As the Admin, I want to type the name admin and see a PIN field, so that only someone who knows the PIN gets Admin controls.
7. As the Admin, I want a wrong PIN rejected with a clear message, so that I know to try again.
8. As the Admin, I want the device to remember that I'm the Admin until I switch name, so that I don't enter the PIN every day.
9. As a Member, I want to be prevented from using the name admin without the PIN, so that nobody accidentally gets Admin controls.

Order List lifecycle

10. As the Admin, I want to open today's Order List, so that Members can start adding Items.
11. As the Admin, I want opening today's Order List to lock any older Order List that is still open, so that nobody keeps adding to a past day.
12. As the Admin, I want to lock the Order List when I go to buy, so that the list doesn't change while I'm shopping.
13. As the Admin, I want to unlock a Locked Order List, so that I can let a late Member add something.
14. As the Admin, I want to be unable to open a second Order List for the same day, so that there is only ever one list per day.
15. As a Member, I want to see a status pill (Open / Locked / No list today), so that I know whether I can still order.
16. As a Member, I want the add box and remove buttons disabled when the Order List is Locked or there is no list today, so that I don't try changes that will fail.
17. As a Member, I want my add or remove to be refused, with a message, if the Admin locked the Order List a moment before, so that the Admin's locked list never changes behind their back.

Adding and removing Items

18. As a Member, I want to type an Item name and press add, so that I can order something new.
19. As a Member, I want Catalog suggestions as I type, so that I reuse an existing Item instead of creating a near-duplicate.
20. As a Member, I want an exact case-insensitive match to reuse the existing Item, so that "Bag of chips" and "bag of chips" are one Item.
21. As a Member, I want a new name to join the Catalog automatically, so that teammates can pick it later.
22. As a Member, I want leading/trailing spaces ignored in Item names, so that stray spaces don't create duplicates.
23. As a Member, I want empty Item names rejected, so that blank Items never reach the Catalog.
24. As a Member, I want "Your usuals" chips showing Items I ordered before, so that I can add my regular order with a tap.
25. As a Member, I want "Everything else" chips showing the rest of the Catalog, so that I can pick what teammates have ordered.
26. As a Member, I want tapping a chip to add that Item to my Order, so that picking is one tap.
27. As a Member, I want to add the same Item twice to get two, so that I can order more than one without a quantity field.
28. As a Member, I want "My order" listing each Item I added with a remove button while the Order List is Open, so that I can fix mistakes.
29. As a Member, I want removing one of two identical Items to remove only one, so that I can go from two to one.

Visibility

30. As a Member, I want to see only my own Order, so that the screen stays about what I want.
31. As a Member, I want my Order and the list status to update live, so that I see the Admin's lock or unlock without refreshing.
32. As the Admin, I want an Admin card at the top of the same screen, so that my controls sit beside my own Order.
33. As the Admin, I want to order like any Member, so that I can get my own food on the same list.
34. As the Admin, I want a Shopping view with each Item and its total count across all Orders, so that I can buy without tallying.
35. As the Admin, I want a By member view listing each Member's Order, so that I can hand out the food.
36. As the Admin, I want the Shopping and By member views to update live, so that late additions show up while I check.
37. As the Admin, I want a History view of past Order Lists, so that I can look back at what was ordered.
38. As the Admin, I want each past Order List to show its Shopping and By member views read-only, so that history can't be changed.
39. As a Member, I want no access to History or other Members' Orders, so that the Admin's views stay the Admin's.

Platforms and delivery

40. As a Member on a laptop, I want to use OrderList in the browser, so that I don't need to install anything.
41. As a Member on Android, I want to install OrderList as an app from an EAS internal-distribution link, so that it lives on my home screen.
42. As a Member on Android, I want fixes to arrive through EAS Update, so that I don't reinstall the APK for every change.
43. As a Member, I want the same screen and behavior on web and Android, so that switching devices is painless.
44. As a Member, I want a clear error when a change fails (for example, no connection), so that I don't think an Item was added when it wasn't.

Operation

45. As the Admin, I want to change the PIN in the Firebase console, so that I can rotate it without a new app release.
46. As the Admin, I want the Security Rules written explicitly (not test-mode), so that the app doesn't stop working when test-mode Rules expire after 30 days.

## Implementation Decisions

Decisions carried from charting (epic OrderList-yvz and its children):

- Platforms: web + Android. No iOS.
- Backend: Firebase Spark, Firestore only, through the Firebase JS SDK (Expo's recommendation for universal apps). No Firebase Auth: nobody signs in to Firebase. No Cloud Functions, no API routes.
- Hosting and delivery: web on EAS Hosting Free (the app already uses server output); Android as an EAS internal-distribution APK plus EAS Update. The team stays at 20 devices or fewer.
- Live updates through Firestore snapshot listeners; no manual refresh.
- Online only, no offline mode (decided by the user, 2026-11-02). Firestore keeps its default memory-only cache; no persistent offline cache is enabled. User story 44 covers what a Member sees when a change fails.
- Admin check: the Admin types the name admin, then a PIN. The PIN lives in a Firestore config document, edited in the Firebase console. The app reads it and compares in the client; a match reveals the Admin card. Anyone determined can read the PIN: accepted.
- Security Rules: explicit, checked into the repo. Open reads and writes for all clients, except: (a) the PIN config document is client-read-only; (b) any write to an Order is refused while its Order List is Locked (one get() on the Order List). Reads, writes and Admin-only actions are otherwise not enforced by Rules.
- Screens (prototype variant A, chosen): a name-entry screen (typing admin reveals a PIN field) and one scrolling Order screen for everyone: greeting with name + status pill; type-to-add box with Catalog suggestions; "Your usuals" chips then "Everything else" chips; "My order" with remove buttons while Open. The Admin gets an extra card at the top with open / lock / unlock and a Shopping / By member / History switch; the Admin's own Order sits below like any Member's. The prototype lives on the local branch prototype/screens (route /prototype-screens?variant=A) and is reference only, never merged.
- No quantities, no Reorder, no money, no "bought"/"unavailable" marking, no Catalog cleanup.

Spec-level decisions (made while writing this spec; change them freely before building):

- The starter tabs (Home/Explore) are removed. The app becomes a stack with two routes: name entry and the Order screen. The Order screen redirects to name entry when no name is remembered.
- Member key: a Member is identified by their name, trimmed and lower-cased. The name as first typed is kept for display. The key admin is reserved for the Admin; choosing it requires the PIN.
- Device memory: the remembered name and the Admin flag live in an Expo-recommended key-value store that works on web and Android. Because web is server-rendered, nothing reads device storage at module scope.
- "Today": the Admin device's local date (YYYY-MM-DD) when opening; it is the Order List's id. Open is offered only when today has no Order List; otherwise the Admin card offers lock or unlock for today's list.
- Opening today's Order List locks any older Order List still Open, in the same write batch.
- Firestore shape:
  - Order List: one document per day, id = the date, with status (open | locked) and timestamps.
  - Order: the Order List's order lines, one document per added Item instance, holding the Member key, Member display name, Item id, Item display name and added time. Adding the same Item twice creates two lines; remove deletes one line. A Member's Order is their lines in that Order List; the Shopping view groups all lines by Item; By member groups them by Member.
  - Catalog: one document per Item, id = the trimmed, lower-cased name, holding the display name as first entered. Adding an Item creates the Catalog document only if absent, which gives the case-insensitive reuse for free.
  - Usual Items: one document per Member key listing the Item ids that Member has ordered; adding an Item adds its id. "Your usuals" = those Items; "Everything else" = the rest of the Catalog.
  - Admin config: one document holding the PIN.
- The Rules' Locked check applies to order-line documents nested under their Order List, so the get() path is the parent document.
- One data module owns all Firestore access. Screens never import Firestore directly. Its interface (names indicative):
  - Admin: check the PIN; open today's Order List; lock and unlock an Order List; watch the Shopping and By member views of any Order List; list past Order Lists.
  - Member: watch the current Order List's status; add an Item by name (normalizes, reuses or creates the Catalog Item, records the line, updates usual Items); remove one line; watch my Order; watch the Catalog split into usuals and everything else.
  - Suggestions are filtered in the client from the watched Catalog (the Catalog is small).
  - The module takes the Firestore instance and a clock ("today") as inputs, so tests can point it at the emulator and fix the date.
- Firebase web config comes from public Expo environment variables; it is not a secret.
- The Firebase project, Firestore database, PIN document and Rules deployment are set up by a person (console + Firebase CLI), not by the app.

## Testing Decisions

- Seam (agreed with the user): one seam, the Firestore data module, tested with Jest against the Firebase Local Emulator Suite (Firestore emulator) with the project's real Security Rules loaded. One seam covers both the app logic and the Rules: a write to a Locked Order List is refused through the module, exactly as in the app.
- Test runner: set up following Expo's "Unit Testing with Jest" guide (jest-expo). None exists yet. The emulator needs firebase-tools and a Java runtime locally; tests run inside the emulator wrapper command, and each test starts from an empty database (emulator data-clear endpoint).
- A good test drives the module's public interface only and asserts on what a Member or the Admin would observe (my Order, the Shopping totals, the status, a refused write), never on document paths or field names, so the Firestore shape can change without rewriting tests.
- Behaviors to cover:
  - Opening today's Order List; opening when an older list is still Open locks it; no second list for the same day.
  - Lock and unlock change the status seen by watchers.
  - Adding an Item: new name joins the Catalog; case/space variants reuse the existing Item; empty names are rejected; the same Item twice appears twice in my Order and counts 2 in Shopping.
  - Removing one of two identical lines leaves one.
  - Adding or removing while Locked is refused (Rules), and allowed again after unlock.
  - The PIN document can't be written by a client; a correct PIN passes the check and a wrong one fails.
  - My Order shows only my lines; By member groups lines per Member; name matching is case-insensitive.
  - Usual Items: after ordering an Item, it appears in my usuals and not in my "Everything else".
  - History lists past Order Lists, and their views stay readable.
- Not tested in v1: screen components (kept thin over the module), EAS builds and updates. These are checked by hand on the physical Android device the developer has connected over USB; no Android emulator is needed. That device does not replace the Firestore emulator: the Jest tests run in Node on the computer, not on the phone.
- Prior art: none. The repo is still the Expo starter with no tests.

## Out of Scope

- iOS.
- Firebase Auth of any kind (Admin email/password, anonymous Members, Google sign-in).
- Rules that enforce Admin-only actions or per-Member ownership (loose security is deliberate).
- Notifications when the Admin opens an Order List (feasible later at $0 with one EAS API route + Expo Push; branch research/notification-feasibility).
- Money tracking, quantities, Catalog cleanup (README "Ideas for later"), Reorder, real accounts, "bought"/"unavailable" marking.
- A web manifest / home-screen web app on Android, and Play Console distribution.
- Offline mode: the app is online only.

## Further Notes

- Expo SDK 58: per AGENTS.md, fetch the versioned Expo docs before using any Expo API, and add packages with npx expo install.
- The React Compiler is on: don't add memoization by reflex.
- If Firebase Auth returns later, the documented React Native persistence path has a known TypeScript export issue (firebase-js-sdk#9316).
- Research and decisions: epic OrderList-yvz (children yvz.1–yvz.6); branches research/backend-hosting, research/android-delivery, research/notification-feasibility, prototype/screens. Never push: the repo has no git remote.

title: How does the Admin prove they are the Admin in Firebase?
description:
## Question

v1 has one Admin who unlocks Admin actions (open, lock and unlock an Order List) with a PIN (OrderList-yvz.1). The backend is now Firebase Spark with the JS SDK and no server code (OrderList-yvz.5), so a PIN check would have to live in Security Rules, which is awkward. Should the Admin instead be a Firebase Auth account (e.g. email/password) that Rules check by uid? Do Members need any auth (e.g. anonymous) so Rules can limit writes to their own Order? And where does the Admin's secret live?

comments.author: ahmed
comments.text:
## Answer

No Firebase Auth in v1 (out of scope for now). This drops the "Auth" part of OrderList-yvz.5; nobody signs in to Firebase.

- **Admin**: types the name `admin` (OrderList-yvz.1, yvz.4), then a PIN. The PIN is checked in the app only; a match reveals the Admin card. The device remembers the Admin until they switch name.
- **PIN storage**: a Firestore doc, edited in the Firebase console. Clients may read it but not write it (the console bypasses Rules). Anyone determined can read the PIN: accepted under the map's deliberate loose security.
- **Members**: type a name only; no auth (same-name handling as decided in OrderList-yvz.1).
- **Security Rules**: written explicitly (never default test-mode Rules, which expire after 30 days). Open reads/writes for all clients, except: Order writes are refused while their Order List is Locked (one get() on the list), and the PIN doc is client-read-only.

Rejected: Firebase Auth email/password Admin + anonymous Members (deferred, not for v1); PIN enforced in Rules (PIN sent with every write).

Build note: if Firebase Auth returns later, getReactNativePersistence + AsyncStorage is the documented RN persistence path, with a known TS export issue (firebase-js-sdk#9316).

title: Choose the backend, hosting and Android delivery
description:
## Question

Given the research findings, which backend + hosting does v1 use, and how does it reach Android phones?

comments.author: ahmed
comments.text:
## Answer

**Backend: Firebase on the free Spark plan (Firestore + Firebase Auth) through the Firebase JS SDK; the web app on EAS Hosting Free. Android: an EAS internal-distribution APK + EAS Update. Total $0.**

- **Why Firebase over the researched Neon option:** OrderList is a learning project, and the user's upcoming projects use Firebase, so Firestore, Security Rules and Firebase Auth are skills worth learning here. Live updates via onSnapshot come free. Neon + API routes stays the documented alternative (research/backend-hosting).
- **JS SDK (tentative):** web is a v1 target, and Expo's Firebase guide recommends the JS SDK for universal apps. Revisit if the future projects use @react-native-firebase (its web support is unverified).
- **Android:** an APK through EAS internal distribution. Not a home-screen web app, and not Play internal testing: Play Console access exists, but EAS was chosen for learning. The team stays at 20 devices or fewer, so the 2027 free developer-verification cap holds.
- **Admin check:** a PIN in Security Rules is awkward. How the Admin proves they are the Admin graduates to its own ticket.
- **Out of v1, feasible later at $0:** the Admin starts a list and the team is notified. This needs one EAS API route, because Spark has no Cloud Functions; the route sends a batch to Expo Push, with the FCM V1 key uploaded to EAS. Google sign-in in an APK needs a native module. Findings: branch research/notification-feasibility, docs/research/notification-feasibility.md.

title: How should the Member and Admin screens look and flow?
description:
## Question

What are the screens and flows for v1: name entry, the Member's Order screen (type-to-add with Catalog suggestions, Catalog with own past Items first), and the Admin's open/lock/unlock controls, shopping view, per-Member view and history? Rough prototype to react to.

comments.author: ahmed
comments.text:
## Answer

**Variant A: one scrolling screen**, chosen by the user after trying all three on web (desktop + Android Chrome). No changes requested.

- **Member** (top to bottom): greeting with name + Order List status pill (Open / Locked / No list today); type-to-add box with Catalog suggestions as you type; "Your usuals" chips (Items the Member ordered before), then "Everything else" chips, tap to add; "My order" with remove buttons while the list is Open.
- **Admin**: the same screen, plus a card at the top holding the open / lock / unlock action and a Shopping (totals per Item) / By member / History switch. The Admin's own Order sits below, like any Member's.
- **Name entry**: one screen asking for a name; typing `admin` reveals a PIN field.
- **Rejected**: B (tabs per task) and C (Catalog-first tile grid with a bottom order tray).

Prototype (all three variants, never merged): local branch `prototype/screens` (fcf1df6), route `/prototype-screens?variant=A|B|C`. Note: on web the starter's `expo-router/ui` Tabs only register routes that have a TabTrigger inside TabList; routes without one bounce to the first tab.

title: How do Members get the app on Android phones?
description:
## Question

No iOS. What are the options for getting OrderList onto team Android phones (EAS internal-distribution APK, the web app installed to the home screen, Play Console internal testing), what does each cost in setup and per-update effort, and is a native Android build needed at all given the web app runs in the phone browser?

comments.author: ahmed
comments.text:
## Answer

**Recommendation: no native Android build in v1.** Members open the OrderList web app in Chrome on their phones and add it to the home screen (PWA). This needs public/manifest.json linked from src/app/+html.tsx, served over HTTPS, and no service worker. Why: web is already a v1 target, so there is one codebase and one deploy. Changes reach phones on the next page load. It costs $0 beyond the web hosting we need anyway. There is no sideload warning, no Play account, and no exposure to Google's 2027 developer verification. Nothing in the OrderList-yvz.1 decisions needs native features.

Comparison:
• **EAS internal-distribution APK**: eas.json profile with distribution internal, then share the link. Free plan gives 15 Android builds/month and EAS Update to 1K MAUs. JS changes arrive by EAS Update on the next app restart. Native changes need a reinstalled APK. Each Member accepts an unknown-source warning. Android developer verification goes global in 2027 (free limited-distribution accounts are capped at 20 devices; adb installs are unaffected). Best fallback if native is ever needed.
• **Web app on home screen (PWA)**: a manifest plus a +html.tsx link. Free. Updates arrive on reload. No offline use, which is fine because the app needs the server. Hosting for web.output server is decided in OrderList-yvz.5 (EAS Hosting supports it, free plan 100k requests/month).
• **Play Console internal testing**: US$25 one-time Play account, Service Account key for EAS Submit, AAB builds, up to 100 testers via opt-in link, each needing a Google account. Updates arrive within minutes or via EAS Update. Most setup effort.

Open questions: exact developer-verification fees; whether Chrome still needs a service worker for the automatic install prompt (manual Add to home screen works regardless).

Findings: branch research/android-delivery, docs/research/android-delivery.md

title: Which backend and hosting should store the shared Order List?
description:
## Question

Several devices (web + Android) must share one Order List, the Catalog and the Admin PIN. What are the simplest, cheapest backend + hosting options for an Expo SDK 58 app (e.g. Expo Router API routes on EAS Hosting with a hosted DB, Supabase, Firebase), how does each handle live updates vs refresh, what does each cost for a ~small team, and which do you recommend? No hosting constraints exist.

comments.author: ahmed
comments.text:
## Answer

**Recommendation: Expo Router API routes on EAS Hosting Free + Neon Free Postgres ($0/month).** The repo already has web.output "server" and SDK 58 enables API routes by default, so the web host and backend are one `eas deploy`. All rules (Admin PIN, Locked, auto-lock old list, case-insensitive Catalog match) live in TypeScript API routes; the PIN is a server-only EAS secret env var. Trade-off: no live updates (EAS Hosting runs on Cloudflare Workers; WebSockets undocumented) - use refresh-on-focus + pull-to-refresh, optional slow polling on the Admin shopping view; mind the 100k requests/month free limit. Fallback if live updates become a must: Supabase.

Comparison (all $0 for a small team):
- A. API routes + EAS Hosting + Neon: refresh only; PIN checked in API route (EAS secret); medium setup (write ~8-10 routes + SQL). Android needs expo-router `origin` set to deployed URL.
- B. Supabase: live via Realtime postgres_changes; PIN checked in a security-definer Postgres function via rpc(); free project pauses after 1 week idle (Pro $25).
- C. Firestore (Spark): live via onSnapshot; Cloud Functions need Blaze, so PIN check must sit in Security Rules (get() on a hidden doc) - awkward; NoSQL totals computed client-side.
- D. Convex: live built in, free 1M calls/month; partly unverified.
Web hosting is needed in every option (web.output server) - EAS Hosting Free covers it.

Unverified: EAS Hosting WebSocket support, Firestore listener billing, supabase-js on web in this app, Convex details.

Findings: branch research/backend-hosting, docs/research/backend-hosting.md

title: What does v1 do for Admins and Members?
description:
## Question

What does v1 of OrderList do: roles, identity, the Order List lifecycle, how Members add Items, and what each role sees?

comments.author: ahmed
comments.text:
## Answer

Resolved while charting (grilling with the user, 2026-11-01). Terms per GLOSSARY.md.

- **Platforms**: web + Android. No iOS.
- **Admin**: one fixed Admin, signs in with the name `admin` plus a PIN. The Admin is also a Member and can order.
- **Members**: type their name once (remembered on the device); names compare case-insensitively; same-name people must disambiguate ("Ahmed K"). No passwords.
- **Order List lifecycle**: one per day. The Admin opens it; Members add/remove their own Items while it's open; the Admin locks it to go buy, after which Members can't add or remove. The Admin can unlock. Opening a new list auto-locks any still-open old one. No open list means Members can't order.
- **Adding Items**: type the name and press add, with type-ahead suggestions from the Catalog; an exact case-insensitive match reuses the existing Item, otherwise a new Item joins the Catalog. Or pick from the Catalog, which lists the Member's own previously ordered Items first. No Reorder feature.
- **No quantities**: add the same Item twice to get two.
- **Visibility**: Members see only their own Order. The Admin sees a shopping view (totals per Item) and a per-Member view. Only the Admin sees past Order Lists (read-only history).
- **Not in v1** (noted in README "Ideas for later"): money tracking, quantities, Catalog cleanup. No "bought"/"unavailable" marking.

title: Chart OrderList v1
description:
## Destination

A v1 spec, written as a Beads epic, for the OrderList team food-ordering app on web + Android, ready to slice into build tickets.

## Notes

- Domain vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Expo SDK 58 app (see AGENTS.md: fetch versioned Expo docs, never answer from memory).
- Grilling tickets: call the grilling and domain-modeling skills.
- Research findings go on a local `research/<name>` branch. This repo has no git remote: never push.
- Loose security is a deliberate choice for an internal team tool.
- OrderList is a learning project for React Native/Expo and Firebase: prefer choices that teach those over the most convenient option.

## Decisions so far

- [What does v1 do for Admins and Members?](OrderList-yvz.1): web + Android; one Admin (`admin` + PIN); Members type a name; daily Order List opened/locked/unlocked by the Admin; type-or-pick Items from a shared Catalog; no quantities; Members see only their own Order.
- [Which backend and hosting should store the shared Order List?](OrderList-yvz.2): research recommends Expo Router API routes on EAS Hosting Free + Neon Free Postgres ($0); no live updates, so refresh on focus/pull; Supabase if live updates become a must.
- [How do Members get the app on Android phones?](OrderList-yvz.3): research recommends no native build for v1: the web app added to the Android home screen via a web manifest over HTTPS; EAS internal APK + EAS Update as the later fallback.
- [How should the Member and Admin screens look and flow?](OrderList-yvz.4): one scrolling screen for everyone (add box, usuals + Catalog chips, My order); the Admin gets an extra card with open/lock/unlock and Shopping / By member / History.
- [Choose the backend, hosting and Android delivery](OrderList-yvz.5): Firebase Spark (Firestore + Auth, JS SDK) with live updates, chosen over Neon for learning; web on EAS Hosting Free; Android via an EAS internal-distribution APK + EAS Update.
- [How does the Admin prove they are the Admin in Firebase?](OrderList-yvz.6): no Firebase Auth in v1 (drops the Auth part of OrderList-yvz.5); the app checks the `admin` PIN against a client-read-only Firestore doc and remembers it on the device; explicit open Rules, except Order writes are refused while the Order List is Locked.
- Offline: online only, no offline mode (decided by the user, 2026-11-02); recorded in spec OrderList-df2.

## Out of scope

- iOS.
- Money tracking, quantities, Catalog cleanup: v1 leaves them out (README "Ideas for later").
- Reorder and real accounts: ruled out while charting.
- Notifications when the Admin starts a list, and Google sign-in: out of v1; feasible later at $0 with one EAS API route + Expo Push (branch research/notification-feasibility).
- Firebase Auth (Admin or Member sign-in): not for now; the Admin PIN is checked in the app instead (OrderList-yvz.6).

comments.author: ahmed
comments.text: Destination reached: the v1 spec is epic OrderList-df2 (labelled ready-for-agent).

title: Exclude .worktrees/ from Metro in the main checkout
description: Expo's default Metro blockList (node_modules/@expo/metro-config/build/ExpoMetroConfig.js) does not exclude .worktrees/, so the dev server in the main checkout crawls every ticket worktree including its node_modules. Impact not measured. Fix if it bites: add metro.config.js extending expo/metro-config's getDefaultConfig, appending a blockList regex built from path.resolve(__dirname, '.worktrees') so a worktree's own Metro does not block itself. Found while implementing OrderList-wct.
